classes.name: Testosterone replacement
classes.description: Testosterone gel/solution (AndroGel, Testim, Fortesta, Vogelxo, generic 1%/1.62%), injections (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed undecanoate), patch (Androderm), oral undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex), nasal (Natesto), pellets (Testopel).
classes.plainDescription: Testosterone replacement for low testosterone, as a gel, shot or pill.

preferredAgent.strength: 1.62% gel pump (generic for AndroGel; strength not printed on PDL)
preferredAgent.sig: Apply the labeled starting dose once each morning to clean, dry skin of the shoulders and upper arms (1.62% gel: 40.5 mg; 1% gel: 50 mg); adjust by morning serum testosterone. Let dry, cover the site, and wash hands (label; boxed warning on secondary exposure).
preferredAgent.plainSig: Rub the gel on your shoulders each morning, let it dry, and wash your hands. Keep it away from children and partners.

paRequired.drug: Testosterone topical (generic packets for AndroGel, Axiron, Fortesta, Vogelxo)

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.20 (Endocrine and Metabolic Agents, Androgenic Agents, Topical). Only topical testosterone appears: generic testosterone gel pump (for AndroGel) is Preferred with no PA; brand gels, generic packets and Natesto require PA. The PDL does not print the strength of the generic pump; 1.62% is the strength of the generic AndroGel pump (judgment). Injectable testosterone (cypionate, enanthate, Xyosted, Aveed), oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex), patches and pellets do not appear on this PDL; the testosterone heading is not a PDL class beyond topical agents, so they are covered on the Medicaid formulary and not confirmed here.

preferredAgent.sig: 50-400 mg IM every 2 to 4 weeks, adjusted to keep morning testosterone in the normal range (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot every 2 to 4 weeks; your prescriber sets the dose from blood tests.

records.preferredRestriction: Quantity limit: 4 mL per 28 days (PDF p. 133); no PA printed

alternatives.note: F; QL 10 mL per 28 days (PDF p. 133)
F; QL 5 mL per 28 days (PDF p. 133)

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp. 133-134 (Androgens section and the duplicate listing). Testosterone cypionate 200 mg/mL is F with QL 4 mL per 28 days; that is a controlled substance QL and is recorded in preferredRestriction. Strength choice is a judgment call. Not on the list: Aveed (testosterone undecanoate injection) and Testopel (pellets). Both are clinic-administered and may fall under the medical benefit; the document does not say. Also absent: Xyosted, Jatenzo, Tlando, Natesto, Androderm, Fortesta, Vogelxo, AndroGel brand.

records.preferredRestriction: PA required (printed, PDF p.105). PA criteria are not printed in this document.
records.verificationNote: Read PDF p.105 (formulary p.103). Every testosterone line listed is Tier 1 with PA. The preferred pick is the standard cypionate injection, not an oral or unflagged product, since no testosterone product is free of PA here. Aveed (undecanoate) and Testopel (pellets) are provider-administered and not listed, so they may sit under the medical benefit; not recorded as nonformulary. Xyosted, Jatenzo, Tlando, Kyzatrex, Natesto and Androderm are not listed. Marked partial for the benefit-routing gap.

QL amounts are not printed. Strength and dosing are standard label values. ANDROGEL, XYOSTED, TESTIM, FORTESTA and NATESTO are not listed by brand name. Testopel is not listed by brand name.
